source: apsoai/cli#208, draft 1. This file is the one place the rule list lives: correct a rule here and the suite, the check and `apso test access` follow.

statuses.enforced: The generated service enforces the rule in this language. The suite must run at least one case for it.
statuses.refused: `apso generate` refuses the feature in this language. The suite must run a case that shows the refusal.
statuses.pending: Not built yet. `issue` names the work that builds it and must add the cases.
statuses.na: Does not apply to this language.

rules.rule: The default is no access. A request is refused unless a rule below allows it. A missing setting, an unknown credential or an unrecognised case never opens anything.
Every route needs a valid credential unless it is marked public. The health check is public.
A token is accepted only when its signature, issuer, audience, expiry and algorithm all check out against the issuer's published keys.
A token from an issuer that is not listed is refused. With several issuers, each token is checked only against its own issuer's keys, audience and claim names.
Every accepted request has exactly one kind of caller: a user or a service.
An API key that does not match the chosen key source is refused.
A user caller reads and changes only rows of their own tenant.
rules.note: A scopeBy path through a parent (project.organizationId) is enforced in TypeScript and refused at generate in Python and Go. The scope covers every operation: `apso generate` refuses `scopeOptions.enforceOn`.

rules.rule: Nothing in the query can widen that: not a filter, an `or` group, an embed, a sort or a count, in either query syntax. A TypeScript service accepts the PostgREST syntax only and answers 400 to a nestjsx parameter.
rules.note: A relation between two entities scoped by the same keys loads only rows of the caller's tenant, whatever the stored foreign key names.

rules.rule: On create and update the tenant always becomes the caller's tenant, whatever the body says.
rules.note: No schema option turns this off: `apso generate` refuses `scopeOptions.injectOnCreate`. A foreign key to a tenant-scoped entity must name a row the caller can read, or the write is refused with 403. A service caller can set any tenant and any foreign key.

rules.rule: A user token with no tenant is refused on tenant-scoped entities. The service never looks the tenant up.
Scope is skipped only for roles the schema names, and for service callers.
An operation limited to certain roles is refused to every other role, directly and through a join.
A grant adds a permission in the granting tenant only. It never removes a default, and a caller cannot grant a permission to themselves.
A caller with a valid API key is a service caller. It may call any route and sends its own tenant filter.

The key source is chosen once at start-up from the environment: a key set there, else the platform's gateway token, else keys are off. A key that fails its source is refused, and no other source is tried. With no key source and no sign-in configured, every request is refused.
A valid key at the gateway becomes a signed service token for that one service, valid for about a minute.
rules.platform: The gateway checks the key against the platform's key table and signs the service token.
rules.note: The suite signs service tokens itself, so only the service's half (it accepts a valid token) has cases.

rules.rule: A service token that is expired, changed, or issued for another service is refused.
rules.platform: Only a service the platform deployed is given the gateway's keys to check service tokens against.

rules.rule: A service token header sent from outside is never trusted.
rules.platform: The gateway replaces any service token header a caller sends.
rules.note: The service's half has cases: a token the gateway did not sign is refused.

rules.rule: A request with no key reaches the service, and the service decides.
rules.platform: The gateway lets a request with no key through unchanged.
rules.note: The service's half has cases: with no key, the user token decides.

rules.rule: A browser cannot send the key.
rules.platform: The gateway refuses the key header from browser origins.

rules.rule: No service can read the key table, and the engine refuses to deploy code that has no guard.
rules.platform: The key table is outside every service's database, and the engine checks for the guard before a deploy.

rules.rule: Only operations the schema opts in are tools.
When sign-in is configured, every request to the external MCP address (`/mcp`) needs a valid token issued for it, including listing tools.
A tool call gets the same answer as the same REST call: same sign-in, permission and tenant checks.
Every request, allowed or refused, writes one line with the caller, the request id, the route or tool, and the status.
No token, key or cookie value appears in any log line.
rules.note: API keys have cases today. Tokens and cookies wait for the logging library.

rules.rule: A feature a language cannot enforce is refused by `apso generate` for that language.
rules.note: TypeScript enforces every feature, so it has nothing to refuse.

rules.rule: A schema that cannot be enforced fails at generate: permissions without sign-in, an unprotected grants entity. A tenant scope whose provider maps no tenant claim does not fail: generate warns, and at run time a token with no tenant gets the "no tenant" 403 on tenant-scoped entities, in every language.

The auth entities answer a service caller only. With the `better-auth` provider these are the session, user and membership entities named in the `auth` block, plus Better Auth's other tables. A signed-in user is refused on every one of their routes, no other entity's route loads them through a join or an embed, and `apso generate` refuses `mcp` on them.

MCP tools have one address per audience. `/mcp/internal` exists whenever an entity has `mcp`, with or without sign-in, and answers service callers only: an API key, or the gateway's service token for a key or an Apso user. A user token is not a credential there. `/mcp` exists only when sign-in is configured and answers signed-in users only: an API key or a service token is not a credential there and does not reach the route a tool calls.
